# R App API {.unnumbered} :::: {.callout-warning collapse='false' appearance='default' icon='false'} ## [Caution]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.25em;'} ::: {style='font-size: 1.00em; color: #282b2d;'} This section is being revised. Thank you for your patience. ::: :::: ## Initial launch The application and API need a little attention to get working. When I tried to initially run the app, I get the following error: ```{.default} Warning: Error in httr2::req_perform: Failed to perform HTTP request. Caused by error in `curl::curl_fetch_memory()`: ! Could not connect to server [127.0.0.1]: Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 8080 after 0 ms: Could not connect to server 163: 162: signalCondition 161: signal_abort 160: cnd_signal 159: handle_resp 158: httr2::req_perform 154: eventReactiveValueFunc 102: pred 101: renderText 100: func 87: renderFunc 86: output$pred 1: runApp ``` This is because we need to have the model API running in order to make requests from the app. To do this, I recommend reorganizing the API and app files into separate directories. ::: {.cell} ::: ```{.default} _labs/lab3/R ├── R.Rproj ├── api #<1> │ ├── api.Rproj │ └── mod-api.R #<1> ├── app #<2> │ ├── app-api.R │ └── app.Rproj #<2> ├── eda-db.qmd #<3> └── r-data-load.R #<4> ``` 1. `vetiver` model API 2. `shiny` application 3. EDA of `palmerpenguins` data using `dplyr` and `ggplot2` 4. Load `palmerpenguins` data into `duckdb` ## API The [`labs/lab3/R/api/mod-api.R` file]() contains the following: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # pkgs library(vetiver) library(pins) # connect to model board model_board <- pins::board_folder("../../../lab2/R/models/") # read pinned vetiver model v <- vetiver::vetiver_pin_read(model_board, "penguin_model") # use plumber/vetiver to create router/create API app <- plumber::pr() |> vetiver::vetiver_api(v) ``` ::: ### Start the API The API will keep running when you run the app. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} app |> plumber::pr_run(port = 8080, host = "127.0.0.1") ``` ::: ![`plumber` API for `vetiver` model](img/lab3-r-plumber-router.png){fig-align='center' width='100%'} Now we have a working API! We'll explore the UI in the sections below. Let's launch the app. ## App I've moved the application file (`app-api.R`) into the following directory: ```{.default} _labs/lab3/R/app ├── app-api.R └── app.Rproj 1 directory, 2 files ``` ### Run After opening the `app-api.R` file in a new RStudio session and launching the app I see the following: ![Launch `app-api.R`](img/lab3-r-shiny-launch.png){fig-align='center' width='100%'} But clicking **Predict** originally produced the following error: ```{.default} Warning: Error in httr2::req_perform: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error. ``` In the API session, we also see an error: ```{.default} Error in `hardhat::validate_column_names()`: ! `data` must be a data frame or a matrix, not a list. ``` These errors are pretty clear: The `httr2::req_body_json()` function is sending the data as a JSON list, but the `vetiver` API expects a data frame or a matrix structure. We can fix this in the application server by changing the format of the values sent to the API. ### Reactive values Our error tells us `'data' should be a data frame or a matrix`, so we'll convert `vals()` to a single-row `data.frame` and format the categorical values as numeric (not logical). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} vals <- reactive({ data.frame( bill_length_mm = input$bill_length, species_Chinstrap = as.numeric(input$species == "Chinstrap"), species_Gentoo = as.numeric(input$species == "Gentoo"), sex_male = as.numeric(input$sex == "Male") ) }) ``` ::: ### Predictions The predictions in the server require three changes: 1. The `httr2::req_body_json()` can convert `vals()` into a JSON array structure instead of a flat object (which is the format `vetiver` expects). 2. Add `httr2::req_method("POST")` so the `POST` method is explicit. 3. Finally, we'll create a `response` object and only return `$.pred[1]` (i.e., the predictions). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pred <- eventReactive(input$predict, { request_data <- vals() response <- httr2::request(api_url) |> httr2::req_method("POST") |> httr2::req_body_json(request_data) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json() response$.pred[1] }, ignoreInit = TRUE) ``` ::: A diagram of the reactive flow of User inputs and the **Predict** button API request is below: ```{=html} ``` ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'Input Dependencies' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"16px"}}}%% graph TD subgraph Inputs["User Inputs"] I1("input$bill_length") I2("input$species") I3("input$sex") I4("input$predict") end subgraph Pred["Predict"] Req("request()") --"Creates HTTP
request object"--> Meth("req_method()") Meth --"Changes HTTP
method from
GET to POST"--> BodyJson1("req_body_json()") BodyJson1 --"Converts data.frame
to JSON & sets
request body"--> Perform("req_perform()") Perform --"Sends the HTTP
request to
server & waits
for response"--> BodyJson2("resp_body_json()") end subgraph PredReact["pred()"] Res(["response$.pred[1]"]) end ValsReact(["vals()"]) I1 --> ValsReact I2 --> ValsReact I3 --> ValsReact I4 --"eventReactive()"--> Pred ValsReact --"data.frame"--> BodyJson1 BodyJson2 --"Extracts the
JSON response
body & converts
to R object"--> Res style ValsReact fill:#e1f5fe style PredReact fill:#fff3e0 style Res fill:#e8f5e8 %% style Req fill:#f3e5f5 ``` ## Verify How do we know this API is working? We can change the values in the ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'App & API' %%| fig-align: center %%| eval: false %%| echo: false %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"14px"}}}%% graph TB subgraph Rapi["R Session: API Server"] Mod["Load Model"] --> VetAPI["Create
vetiver_api()"] VetAPI --> Router["pr_run() on
port 8080"] end subgraph Rapp["R Session: Shiny App"] User["User Inputs"] --> Data["Format Data"] Data --> Post["POST to API"] Post --> Pred["Display Prediction"] end Router -.-> Post style Router fill:#e8f5e8 style Post fill:#e1f5fe style Pred fill:#fff3e0 ``` To view the original code in `app-api.R`, expand the section below:
Expand to view app-api.R ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` library(shiny) api_url <- "http://127.0.0.1:8080/predict" ui <- fluidPage( titlePanel("Penguin Mass Predictor"), # Model input values sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel( sliderInput( "bill_length", "Bill Length (mm)", min = 30, max = 60, value = 45, step = 0.1 ), selectInput( "sex", "Sex", c("Male", "Female") ), selectInput( "species", "Species", c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo") ), # Get model predictions actionButton( "predict", "Predict" ) ), mainPanel( h2("Penguin Parameters"), verbatimTextOutput("vals"), h2("Predicted Penguin Mass (g)"), textOutput("pred") ) ) ) server <- function(input, output) { # Input params vals <- reactive( list( bill_length_mm = input$bill_length, species_Chinstrap = input$species == "Chinstrap", species_Gentoo = input$species == "Gentoo", sex_male = input$sex == "Male" ) ) # Fetch prediction from API pred <- eventReactive( input$predict, httr2::request(api_url) |> httr2::req_body_json(vals()) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json(), ignoreInit = TRUE ) # Render to UI output$pred <- renderText(pred()$predict[[1]]) output$vals <- renderPrint(vals()) } # Run the application shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server) ``` ::: :::
